prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations(prefer minor sequence shift, delay upstream not airborne); Adverse Weather(more frequent tactical reviews); Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor extend metering horizon; RFM may combine arrival regulation+departure metering to protect gates for recovery flights); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance; Winter mode(MBO confirms in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity; winter margin before CTT recalc). Actors: Regional Flow Manager(RFM; evaluates arrival regulation via runway, sector load, stands, weather; tactical landing-rate reduction per review interval; staged increase limited until Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing/occupancy), Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor(confirms landing rate; views runway pressure, spacing, crossing points at North/South Runway Meter; protects freezing departure spacing; coordinates Quartzline pad releases), Airport Duty Manager, Ramp Control Lead, Aircraft Operator Representative(acks arrival plan), Airline Operations Coordinator, Slot Coordinator(arrival times via Blueharbor per Business Rules Registry), Network Operations Liaison(coordinates airline control centers on material diversion risk), Emergency Response Coordinator(informed when diversion trigger involves aircraft condition affecting rescue/firefighting), Deicing Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Handling Resource Planner, Meteorology Briefing Officer. Diversion triggers monitored continuously: holding beyond fuel thresholds, approach capability loss, sector saturation, runway below min safe rate. Halcyon logs push rationale. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(syncs display with Time Synchronization Service). Parts: Integrated Tactical Management Position(primary workstation; combined view); Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(triggers regulation when demand>Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT; Ground Delay Program; emergency>scheduled>GA); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(arrival plan, acks to Collaborative Decision Log); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(TOBT; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Nightjar=Arrival Regulation Console(alert before holding stacks); Audit Event Ledger(rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, effective times); Performance Analytics Warehouse(compares predicted holding, airborne delay, diversions, landing rates, throughput, compliance); Sector Load Monitor; Weather Ingest Gateway; Business Rules Registry; Alert Distribution Hub; Common Situation Display(map,

New part:
S426: Emberline sends revised departure metering advisories when runway demand exceeds the configured queue threshold.
S427: Skylark must refresh the apron movement layer within five seconds of each validated surface event.
S428: The Slot Allocation Engine produces the Pushback Window Token when the agreed departure window is frozen for tactical execution.
S429: The Airport CDM Portal exposes agreed Target Off Block Time values and stakeholder remarks to the tactical position in read-only mode unless the operator has an assigned coordination role.
S430: The Demand Prediction Service continuously updates short-term traffic forecasts using the Flight Intent Message stream and recent airport performance history.
S431: The Capacity Assessment Module recalculates available capacity when runway configuration, weather category, staffing assumptions, or sector workload changes.
S432: The Airspace Sector Planner monitors sector demand through the Sector Load Monitor and confirms whether proposed measures are compatible with en route capacity.
S433: The Military Airspace Liaison can mark an airspace release or closure assumption for review before it affects tactical flow calculations.
S434: The Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies weather impacts shown from the Weather Ingest Gateway before the position applies weather-driven capacity values.
S435: The Airport Duty Manager can declare Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State from the tactical header after coordination is complete.
S436: When the operating state changes, the Business Rules Registry supplies the applicable thresholds for alerting, approval routing, and measure publication.
S437: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative review proposed timing changes in the same timeline used by flow staff, which reduces duplicate verbal coordination.
S438: The Ground Handling Dispatcher uses the Handling Resource Planner view to compare planned off-block demand with available servicing capacity at affected stands.
S439: The Gate Conflict Detector highlights stand conflicts that would undermine a proposed departure recovery plan or compress arrival unloading capacity.
S440: A Tactical Regulation Proposal can be drafted directly from the display, checked against current capacity assumptions, and routed through the Alert Distribution Hub for stakeholder acknowledgement.
S441: Accepted adjustments are reflected as Calculated Takeoff Time updates, Slot Compliance State changes, or airport capacity annotations depending on the measure type.
S442: Every operator action, system recommendation, acknowledgement, and rejected alternative is written to the Collaborative Decision Log and the Audit Event Ledger for traceability and post-operation analysis.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
